prompt: Two-pipeline application-managed buffer bridge C++ app using qti::AppSrc and qti::AppSink. Pipeline 1 generates synthetic videotestsrc ball-pattern frames at NV12/1920x1080/30fps into an AppSink with set_buffer_consumer() forwarding buffers. Pipeline 2 receives them via AppSrc (do-timestamp, block, TIME format) and renders fullscreen on waylandsink. Demonstrates cross-pipeline buffer bridging via application code rather than a single linked pipeline.

Audio classification C++ app over an MP4-muxed FLAC track: qtdemux splits concurrent video and audio branches, queues each dynamic pad before parsing/decoding, decodes H.264 video and FLAC audio, converts audio to 16 kHz LMFE features with qtimlaconverter, runs YAMNet CPU inference and qtimlpostprocess(module=yamnet, results=3), renders an RGBA classification panel into qtivcomposer, and displays the video plus panel on Wayland. Uses queue isolation after demux and FLAC decode, 31200-byte audiobuffersplit, and fixed composer panel geometry.

CPU YAMNet audio classification C++ app over an MP4-muxed FLAC track. Queues concurrent qtdemux video/audio branches and the decoded audio path, extracts 16 kHz LMFE features, runs qtimltflite with delegate=none, renders a fixed RGBA 368x64 label panel, and composites it over decoded H.264 video with qtivcomposer for Wayland. Does not set composer pad position/dimensions because that combination deadlocks CPU audio preroll; uses runtime-expanded HOME paths.

isp-camera preview C++ app: captures live frames from the default Qualcomm camera (qtiqmmfsrc), normalizes to NV12/1920x1080/30fps via VideoFilter stream filter, and renders fullscreen on waylandsink with sync disabled for live camera. No AI, no encode, no tee branches. This is the canonical minimal camera-preview shape.

Camera capture encoded to MP4 file C++ app, no display, no AI. Captures isp-camera (qtiqmmfsrc) frames at NV12/1920x1080/30fps, encodes via v4l2h264enc (dmabuf io modes), parses H.264, muxes into mp4mux, writes to filesink with eos handling enabled. This is the canonical camera-to-file record shape with no preview branch.

ISP camera YOLOv5 object-detection C++ app fanning one overlaid stream out to three simultaneous sinks: Wayland display, an MP4 file, and an RTSP mount point (rtspsrc-served rtsp://<device-ip>:8900/live). Captures qticamsrc camera=0 at NV12/1920x1080/30fps, runs YOLOv5 (mapped to qtimlpostprocess module=yolov8 per model-catalog) with bbox-stabilization on HTP/NPU, merges detection metadata with qtimetamux, overlays boxes with qtivoverlay, then tees the overlaid stream into a display branch (sync=false) plus two independent v4l2h264enc(capture-io-mode=4,output-io-mode=5 for camera-native DMA import) encode branches feeding filesink and qtirtspbin respectively. Use for camera-source detection with simultaneous display+file+RTSP output.

This is the base/canonical single-stage YOLOv8 object detection C++ app: qti::Pipeline camera app running YOLOv8 detection on frames from the default isp-camera, then displaying results. Captures qtiqmmfsrc camera=0 at NV12/1920x1080/30fps, tees into a qtimlvconverter to qtimltflite (external delegate, htp) to qtimlpostprocess (module=yolov8) branch, merges detection metadata with qtimetamux, overlays boxes via qtivoverlay, renders fullscreen on waylandsink. Explicit-style Element/Pipeline construction with named link() call.

Fused ML-bin YOLOv8 object detection C++ app from isp-camera to display, using the single qti::MLVideoTFLiteBin wrapper instead of discrete qtimlvconverter/qtimltflite/qtimlpostprocess stages. Captures qtiqmmfsrc camera=0 at NV12/1920x1080/30fps, runs qtimlvideotflitebin (inference-delegate=external, htp, postprocess-module=yolov8) directly in the media path, overlays via qtivoverlay, displays on waylandsink. Use for the compact ML-bin camera detection shape rather than discrete-stage detection.

Two-stage daisy-chain C++ app from an MP4 file to Wayland display: stage 1 runs YOLOX object detection (qtimlvconverter mode=image-batch-non-cumulative, qtimlpostprocess module=yolov8) on full frames and merges its metadata with metamux_1; stage 2 runs MobileNet-v2 classification (qtimlvconverter mode=roi-batch-cumulative, qtimlpostprocess module=mobilenet) on the stage-1 detected ROIs and merges its metadata with metamux_2; a single qtivoverlay draws both bounding boxes and per-object classification labels. Two-mux two-tee topology for detect-then-classify daisy chains (as opposed to detect-then-pose, which uses the HRNet cascade shape).

Event-triggered recording C++ app: decode an MP4 file, run YOLOX object detection on the HTP/NPU, display the detection overlay, and record the composed annotated video to an MP4 only while a person is present. The metadata branch uses qtimlpostprocess text/x-raw constrained by TextFilter and a qti::AppSink gate; a resident is-live qti::AppSrc recording pipeline stays PLAYING and receives moved DMA-backed qti::Buffer frames only while the gate is active, then finalizes mp4mux with EOS. Uses qtimlpostprocess module=yolov8, qtivcomposer, NV12 encoder output, and capture/output IO mode 4/4. HOME-relative paths are resolved at runtime. Use for event-triggered recording and metadata-gated AppSrc/AppSink bridges.

Object detection C++ app from mp4-file to display with a custom C++ postprocess callback instead of the built-in qtimlpostprocess module. Decodes MP4/H.264 via filesrc, qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec, tees into a qtimlvconverter to qtimltflite (yolov8 model) branch feeding a qti::MLPostprocess element with set_handler() implementing manual tensor decode, NMS, and MLDetection population, merges metadata with qtimetamux, overlays via qtivoverlay, displays on waylandsink. Use when the postprocess decode logic must be hand-written in C++ rather than using a built-in module.

Two-stage pose estimation daisy-chain C++ app from mp4-file to display: stage 1 person/object detection (qtimltflite, yolov5m model) with a custom C++ MLPostprocess callback producing detection boxes, stage 2 HRNet pose estimation (qtimltflite, hrnet_pose model) on stage-1 ROIs with a second custom C++ MLPostprocess callback producing keypoints. Both stages use discrete qtimlvconverter/qtimltflite stages, tee/qtimetamux metadata merge per stage, final qtivoverlay renders skeleton keypoints on waylandsink. Use for hand-written pose decode logic instead of a built-in pose postprocess module.

Object detection C++ app from mp4-file to display with a custom C++ preprocess callback inside the fused ML-bin, using qti::MLVideoTFLiteBin.set_preprocess_handler() with preprocess-engine=none instead of a discrete MLVConverter. Decodes MP4/H.264 via filesrc, qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec, mlbin runs the custom NV12-to-tensor conversion plus yolov8 inference and built-in postprocess, overlays via qtivoverlay, displays on waylandsink. Use for hand-written ML-bin preprocess instead of a discrete external-preprocess pipeline.

Object detection C++ app from mp4-file to display with a custom C++ preprocess callback replacing the built-in qtimlvconverter tensor conversion. Decodes MP4/H.264 via filesrc, qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec, tees into a qti::MLVConverter (engine=none) with set_handler() implementing manual NV12-to-tensor conversion, feeds qtimltflite (yolov8 model) and the built-in qtimlpostprocess module, merges metadata with qtimetamux, overlays via qtivoverlay, displays on waylandsink. Use when the image-to-tensor conversion math must be hand-written in C++.

Face detection C++ app from an MP4 file to Wayland display using Face Detection Lite (qtimlpostprocess module=qfd) on HTP/NPU external delegate. Standard single-stage tee/qtimlvconverter/qtimltflite/qtimlpostprocess/TextFilter/qtimetamux/qtivoverlay overlay shape drawing face bounding boxes. Plain face detection only — does not chain into landmark/3DMM/recognition stages; use the face-recognition daisy-chain pattern (qfd -> lite-3dmm -> qfr) instead when the request asks for identity/recognition, not just detection.

Hand gesture recognition C++ app from isp-camera to display: four-stage daisy-chain with palm detection (qtimltflite, palmd module, gpu delegate), qtimetatransform module=roi-palmd for ROI propagation, hand landmark estimation (hlandmark module), gesture embedding (tensor passthrough), and gesture classification (mobilenet module), merged across two qtimetamux stages, overlaid via qtivoverlay onto waylandsink. Explicit-style multi-stage tee/queue wiring named stage_01 through stage_03. Use for the shipped gesture-recognition topology, not a generic N-stage cascade.

Basic single-stage image classification C++ app from an MP4 file to Wayland display: filesrc/qtdemux/h264parse/v4l2h264dec decode, NV12 tee into passthrough and AI branches, discrete qtimlvconverter/qtimltflite/qtimlpostprocess(module=mobilenet) inference on HTP/NPU external delegate, qtimetamux merges the top classification label/confidence text metadata with the passthrough video, qtivoverlay draws it, waylandsink displays fullscreen. Canonical single-stage classification-overlay shape.

Semantic segmentation C++ app from an MP4 file to Wayland display using DeepLabV3+ Mobilenet (module=deeplab-argmax). Tees decoded NV12 video into a passthrough branch feeding qtivcomposer sink_0 directly and an AI branch (qtimlvconverter/qtimltflite HTP/qtimlpostprocess) whose rendered RGBA mask feeds sink_1 with alpha=0.5 blended over the passthrough. No qtimetamux/qtivoverlay because segmentation is a video-output-only postprocess module. Canonical direct-to-composer segmentation shape for a single overlay (not a multi-tile grid).

C++ app that both overlays and app-side-parses AI detection metadata from an MP4 file: after qtimlpostprocess(module=yolov8) produces serialized text/x-raw detection metadata, a second tee (meta_split) fans the metadata into a display branch (TextFilter -> qtimetamux -> qtivoverlay -> waylandsink) and an application-side qti::AppSink branch whose set_buffer_consumer callback receives the raw serialized buffer for app-specific parsing (placeholder logs buffer size; real parsing of the serialized GstStructure is a TODO). Use when the request needs both a visible overlay and programmatic access to detection metadata, not just one or the other.

Two-stage PPE personal protective equipment daisy-chain C++ app using fused ML-bin stages from mp4-file to display. Stage 1 person-foot detection using qtimlvideotflitebin with postprocess-module=qpd and model foot_track_net on full frames. Stage 2 PPE gear detection using qtimlvideotflitebin with postprocess-module=yolov8 and model gear_guard_net on stage-1 person ROIs, preprocess-mode=roi-batch-cumulative. Uses v4l2h264dec hardware decode, qtivoverlay renders both stages results, waylandsink fullscreen display. Direct mlbin1 to mlbin2 to overlay to display fused chain, no external tee/metamux metadata branch.

Non-fused ML-bin YOLOv8 object detection C++ app from mp4-file to display using qti::MLVideoTFLiteBin. Decodes MP4/H.264 via filesrc, qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec hardware decode with dma io modes, normalizes to NV12, runs qtimlvideotflitebin (inference-delegate=external, htp, postprocess-module=yolov8) directly in the media path, overlays via qtivoverlay, renders on waylandsink fullscreen. File-source variant of the fused ML-bin detection shape.

Monocular depth estimation C++ app (MiDaS-v2) with side-by-side comparison on a Wayland display. Decodes an MP4 file through qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec and a post-decoder queue, normalizes to NV12, then tees the video into a passthrough composer pane and a qtimlvconverter -> qtimltflite (midas_v2_w8a8, external HTP/NPU) -> qtimlpostprocess(module=midas-v2, monodepth.json labels) rendered-video branch. The rendered branch uses VideoFilter(RGBA) without pinned resolution and feeds qtivcomposer; composer input pads set vector position/dimensions for the 960x1080 panes. HOME-relative filesystem paths are expanded in C++ before assigning element properties. Displays the composed 1920x1080 result on waylandsink.

32-stream non-batched YOLOX object-detection AI wall C++ app: one MP4 file replicated into 32 fully independent decode/tee/qtimlvconverter/qtimltflite/qtimlpostprocess/qtimetamux/qtivoverlay branches (own inference instance per stream, no qtibatch/qtimldemux sharing), each feeding a dedicated qtivcomposer sink pad tiled into a 6x6 grid (ceil(sqrt(32))) on waylandsink with sync=false. Raises the process file-descriptor limit (setrlimit RLIMIT_NOFILE=10000) before pipeline construction because many independent file-decode branches exhaust the default fd limit. Use for a high-stream-count independent-inference AI wall; use the batched-inference pattern instead when the request calls for shared/batched inference across streams.

Object detection C++ app from an MP4 file to an output MP4 file (no display): decodes with the hardware H.264 decoder, runs YOLOX detection (qtimlpostprocess module=yolov8, confidence 51.0) on HTP/NPU, overlays boxes with qtimetamux/qtivoverlay, re-encodes the overlaid NV12 video with v4l2h264enc (capture/output-io-mode=4/4 for a decoded-file source), muxes with mp4mux, and writes to filesink with eos(true) to finalize the MP4. Use for file-in/file-out AI overlay requests instead of a display sink.

Parallel inferencing C++ app: one MP4 decode tees into four independent HTP/NPU AI branches composed into a 2x2 Wayland grid. Classification, top-down qpd→ROI→HRNet pose, and YOLOX detection use separate passthrough buffer-copy branches with qtimetamux/TextFilter/qtivoverlay; DeepLabV3 segmentation uses a local qtivcomposer to alpha-blend an RGBA mask over a copied passthrough tile before feeding the top-level four-input grid. Uses concrete qpd companion assets, fixed 1920x1080 NV12 input, htp_performance_mode=2, and matching composer geometry.

Top-down HRNet pose estimation C++ app from an MP4 file to Wayland display: stage 1 person-foot detection using person_foot_detection_w8a8 with qtimlpostprocess module=qpd and qtimlvconverter mode=image-batch-non-cumulative generates person ROIs; stage 1 metadata merges with the video, then stage 2 qtimlvconverter mode=roi-batch-cumulative feeds hrnetpose_w8a8 with module=hrnet and hrnet settings, merges stage-2 pose metadata, and qtivoverlay renders skeleton keypoints. Uses external HTP/NPU inference, runtime-expanded HOME paths, and two qtimetamux stages. Use this cascade rather than full-frame HRNet when subjects need ROI pose detection.

MP4 file decode-to-display C++ app using qtdemux/h264parse/v4l2h264dec hardware decode, no AI. Reads local mp4-file, demuxes and parses H.264, decodes via hardware v4l2h264dec with dma io modes, normalizes to NV12, renders fullscreen on waylandsink. Uses the start()/wait()/stop() staged lifecycle instead of execute(). This is the canonical multimedia-only file playback shape with no ML/tee/overlay branches.

Super-resolution C++ app (QuickSRNetLarge) with side-by-side comparison on a Wayland display. Decodes an MP4 file through qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec and a post-decoder queue, normalizes to NV12, then tees the video into an original passthrough composer pane and a qtimlvconverter -> qtimltflite (quicksrnetlarge_w8a8, external HTP/NPU) -> qtimlpostprocess(module=srnet) rendered-video branch. The SR render branch uses VideoFilter(RGBA) and composer input pads set vector position/dimensions for 960x1080 panes; HOME-relative input/model paths are expanded in C++ before element properties. Displays the composed original and upscaled frames on waylandsink.

Tensor dump / inspection C++ app from mp4-file, no display, no postprocess. Decodes MP4/H.264 via filesrc, qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec hardware decode, normalizes to NV12, runs qtimlvconverter to produce a raw model-input tensor (TensorFilter type=UINT8, dimensions 1x520x520x3), writes the tensor buffer to a raw file via multifilesink instead of running inference. Use for capturing/inspecting the exact preprocessed tensor a model would receive, without running qtimltflite.

USB/V4L2 camera preview C++ app: captures a live USB UVC webcam via v4l2src with a device-node argument (default /dev/video2), applies qtivtransform, restricts the stream to NV12/1920x1080/30fps via VideoFilter, renders fullscreen on waylandsink with sync disabled. This is the canonical usb-camera preview shape, distinct from the isp-camera qtiqmmfsrc preview app.

USB camera C++ app with YOLOv8 object detection and simultaneous multi-output: captures a UVC v4l2src YUY2 stream, converts it through qtivtransform to NV12, runs qtimlvconverter -> qtimltflite external HTP/NPU -> qtimlpostprocess(module=yolov8) with qtimetamux/qtivoverlay, then tees the overlaid stream to Wayland display, MP4 recording, and qtirtspbin at /live. Uses one queued passthrough link into qtimetamux, runtime-expanded HOME model/labels paths, and 4/4 encoder IO after the transformed USB stream.

Synthetic test video source with string-form StreamFilter caps and geometric transform, C++ app to display. Generates videotestsrc ball-pattern frames, applies qtivtransform rotate=180, uses raw caps-string qti::StreamFilter objects (video/x-raw,format=NV12,width=1920,height=1080,framerate=30/1 then a resize caps string) instead of the VideoFilter builder, renders on waylandsink fullscreen. Use when raw GStreamer caps strings are needed instead of the typed VideoFilter wrapper.

Runs a QIM SDK C++ pipeline entirely from an external YAML configuration file passed as a command-line argument, with no hand-coded topology in main.cc. Reads the YAML file into a string, constructs a qti::Pipeline directly from the YAML config text via the two-argument Pipeline constructor, and executes it. Use for the YAML-config-driven C++ app pattern where the pipeline topology and properties live entirely in an external YAML file rather than being expressed as Element/Pipeline calls.

12-stream batched YOLOv8 object-detection AI wall C++ app from one MP4 file to a Wayland display. 12 independent decode chains are grouped 4-at-a-time into 3 batch groups; each group shares ONE qtimltflite HTP/NPU inference instance via qtibatch (mux 4 streams) / qtimldemux (split back to 4 per-stream results), avoiding 12 independent HTP graphs (error 6020). Each stream keeps its own qtimlpostprocess(module=yolov8, confidence 51.0) rendering an RGBA detection mask, plus its own raw passthrough branch off the per-stream tee; both feed interleaved qtivcomposer sink pads (2*i passthrough, 2*i+1 mask, same position/dimensions) tiled 4x3. Round-robins htp_device_id across HTP cores, raises RLIMIT_NOFILE, waylandsink sync=false. Two device-verified construction rules: the batch-group demux is named mldemux_<g> (never demux_<g>) to avoid a name collision with the per-stream qtdemux elements named demux_0..demux_11, and BOTH tee legs (split->qpass and split->qai) are linked with separate explicit pipeline.link() calls. Use for shared/batched inference across many streams; use the non-batched yolox grid instead for one independent inference instance per stream.

Single-batch-group batched YOLOv8 object-detection C++ app from one MP4 file to a Wayland display: 4 decode streams share ONE qtimltflite HTP/NPU inference instance via qtibatch (mux 4 streams) / qtimldemux (split back to 4 per-stream results). Each stream keeps its own qtimlpostprocess(module=yolov8, confidence 51.0) RGBA detection mask plus a raw passthrough branch off its tee; both feed interleaved qtivcomposer sink pads (2*i passthrough, 2*i+1 mask) tiled 4x1. This is the minimal one-group shape of the batched multi-stream pattern (stack-local qti::Element wrappers, pipeline.execute()). Two device-verified construction rules: the batch demux is named mldemux_0 (never demux_0) to avoid colliding with per-stream qtdemux demux_0..demux_3, and BOTH tee legs (split->qpass and split->qai) are linked with separate explicit pipeline.link() calls. Use for a small batched-inference wall or as the reference for the batch pattern before scaling to multiple groups.
C++ qimsdk external PoseNet pose-estimation postprocess reference using application-authored tensor decoding, keypoint extraction, skeleton links, and custom NMS.

Single-stream face detection C++ app, file-to-file: decodes an MP4 file with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, runs Face Detection Lite (face-det-lite-w8a8.dlc) inference on full frames via qtimlsnpe on the SNPE runtime DSP (Hexagon) delegate with an explicit tensors=<heatmap,bbox,landmark> output filter (the three tensors module=qfd requires for caps negotiation), decodes detections with qtimlpostprocess module=qfd, overlays bounding boxes on detected faces via qtivoverlay, re-encodes with v4l2h264enc, and writes the result to an output MP4 file via h264parse/mp4mux/filesink. No display sink. SNPE .dlc sibling of the TFLite qfd face-detection app.

Three-stage face recognition daisy-chain C++ app, file-to-file, all stages on the SNPE runtime DSP (Hexagon) delegate: decodes an MP4 file with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, Stage 1 runs Face Detection Lite (face-det-lite-w8a8.dlc) via qtimlsnpe with tensors=<heatmap,bbox,landmark> and module=qfd, Stage 2 runs facial landmark/3DMM alignment (facemap-3dmm-w8a8.dlc, module=lite-3dmm, roi-batch-cumulative) on the Stage 1 ROI, Stage 3 runs face recognition/embedding match (Facial-Attribute-Detection_w8a8.dlc, module=qfr, roi-batch-cumulative) on the Stage 2 aligned ROI. The Stage 3 DLC is a multi-head model whose SNPE default output set emits only the last leaf, so qtimlsnpe sets tensors=<id_feature,liveness_feature,eye_closeness,glasses,mask,sunglasses> to present all six outputs module=qfr requires. Three tee/qtimetamux stages merge each stage's metadata before qtivoverlay; result is re-encoded and written to an output MP4 via mp4mux/filesink. No display sink. Stage 2 lite-3dmm requires /etc/data/{blendShape,meanFace,shapeBasis}.bin on the device. SNPE .dlc sibling of the QNN .bin and ONNX .onnx face-recognition qfr variants.

Six-stream four-stage SNPE/DSP daisy-chain C++ app, file-to-file 3x2 grid: the same MP4 is decoded six times with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, and each stream independently runs the identical four-stage chain - Stage 1 YOLOv8 object detection (yolov8_det_quantized.dlc, qtimlsnpe DSP, tensors=<boxes,scores,class_idx>, module=yolov8) on full frames; Stage 2 DeepLabV3-Plus-MobileNet semantic segmentation (deeplabv3_plus_mobilenet.dlc, qtimlsnpe DSP, module=deeplab-argmax) direct-to-qtivcomposer as an RGBA alpha-blended mask; Stage 3 HRNet pose estimation (hrnet_pose.dlc, qtimlsnpe DSP, module=hrnet, roi-batch-cumulative, settings+results mandatory) on Stage 1 ROIs; Stage 4 Inception-v3 classification (inception_v3.dlc, qtimlsnpe DSP, module=mobilenet) independently on Stage 1 ROIs. Per stream three tee/qtimetamux layers merge Stage 1/3/4 metadata before a qtivoverlay, the segmentation branch feeds a per-stream qtivcomposer directly, and the main_split tee shared with that composer needs a qtivtransform+NV12 private-buffer copy on the overlay leg. The six composited NV12 outputs are tiled into a 3x2 grid by a final qtivcomposer, encoded once and written to a single MP4 via v4l2h264enc/mp4mux/filesink. Heavy stress topology: 24 concurrent DSP inferences plus six decode legs. SNPE .dlc C++ sibling of the Python six-stream daisy-chain.

ISP-camera YOLOv8 object detection C++ app running inference directly on the QNN runtime (qtimlqnn) against a pre-converted QNN cached-binary model (yolov8_det_w8a8.bin), bypassing the TFLite external-delegate indirection. Captures qtiqmmfsrc camera=0 at NV12/1920x1080/30fps, tees into qtimlvconverter -> qtimlqnn (backend=/usr/lib/libQnnHtp.so, system=/usr/lib/libQnnSystem.so, tensors=<boxes,scores,class_idx> output filter) -> qtimlpostprocess module=yolov8 confidence 51.0, merges detection metadata with qtimetamux, overlays boxes via qtivoverlay, renders fullscreen on waylandsink. Direct-QNN-runtime detection where the model ships as a cached .bin rather than a .tflite file. QNN .bin C++ sibling of the TFLite+delegate camera YOLOv8 app.

Six-stream HRNet pose estimation C++ app, file-to-file 3x2 grid, running HRNet (hrnet_pose_w8a8.bin) directly on the full decoded frame of six independent decode instances of the same MP4 via qtimlqnn (QNN native cached .bin runtime, backend=/usr/lib/libQnnHtp.so, system=/usr/lib/libQnnSystem.so) - no detection/ROI-crop stage. Per stream qtimlpostprocess module=hrnet (results=2, labels=hrnet.json, settings=hrnet_settings.json) decodes keypoints, a tee/qtimetamux pair merges pose metadata back onto the video path, and qtivoverlay draws the skeleton. All six overlaid NV12 outputs are tiled into a single 3x2 grid (640x360 cells) by one shared qtivcomposer, hardware-encoded (v4l2h264enc), muxed and written to one output MP4. This HRNet QNN cached-binary model exports a single native output tensor, so qtimlqnn carries no tensors= filter (unlike the multi-tensor YOLOv8 QNN model). High-concurrency topology (six decode legs + six concurrent HTP inferences); raise the device file-descriptor limit. Full-frame native-QNN .bin C++ sibling of the TFLite+delegate HRNet cascade.

Three-stage face recognition daisy-chain C++ app, file-to-file, all stages on the native Qualcomm AI Engine Direct (QNN) runtime loading cached-context .bin models on the HTP/NPU via qtimlqnn (backend=/usr/lib/libQnnHtp.so, system=/usr/lib/libQnnSystem.so). Decodes an MP4 with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, Stage 1 runs Face Detection Lite (face_det_lite_w8a8.bin) with tensors=<heatmap,bbox,landmark> and module=qfd, Stage 2 runs facial landmark/3DMM alignment (facemap_3dmm_w8a8.bin, module=lite-3dmm, roi-batch-cumulative) on the Stage 1 ROI, Stage 3 runs face recognition/embedding match (Facial-Attribute-Detection_w8a8.bin, module=qfr, roi-batch-cumulative) on the Stage 2 aligned ROI. The Stage 3 .bin is a multi-head model whose QNN default output set does not present all six heads, so qtimlqnn sets tensors=<id_feature,liveness_feature,eye_closeness,glasses,mask,sunglasses> to emit all six module=qfr requires. Three tee/qtimetamux stages merge metadata before qtivoverlay; result re-encoded and written to an output MP4 via mp4mux/filesink. No display sink. Stage 2 lite-3dmm requires /etc/data/{blendShape,meanFace,shapeBasis}.bin on the device. QNN .bin sibling of the SNPE .dlc and ONNX .onnx face-recognition qfr variants.

Three-stage face recognition daisy-chain C++ app, file-to-file, all stages on ONNX Runtime (onnxruntime) via qtimlonnx with the CPU execution provider (execution-provider=cpu, optimization-level=disable-all). Decodes an MP4 with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, Stage 1 runs Face Detection Lite (face-det-lite-w8a8-w8a8.onnx, module=qfd), Stage 2 runs facial landmark/3DMM alignment (facemap-3dmm-w8a8-w8a8.onnx, module=lite-3dmm, roi-batch-cumulative) on the Stage 1 ROI, Stage 3 runs face recognition/embedding match (multi-head model.onnx with external weights in model.data, module=qfr, roi-batch-cumulative) on the Stage 2 aligned ROI. Unlike the SNPE/QNN siblings, qtimlonnx has no tensors= property to filter or reorder outputs, so each model's native ONNX output order must directly satisfy qfd's 3-tensor and qfr's 6-tensor contracts; the CPU execution provider is used because it is built into the ONNX Runtime core and portable, whereas the QNN/HTP ONNX Runtime provider plugin is a separate device install, and optimization-level=disable-all preserves the Transpose nodes qtimlonnx uses for layout detection. Three tee/qtimetamux stages merge metadata before qtivoverlay; result written to an output MP4 via mp4mux/filesink. No display sink. The Stage 3 model.onnx needs its model.data sidecar in the same directory; the attribute-only face-attrib-net-w8a8-w8a8.onnx must not be substituted. Stage 2 lite-3dmm requires /etc/data/{blendShape,meanFace,shapeBasis}.bin on the device. ONNX .onnx sibling of the SNPE .dlc and QNN .bin face-recognition qfr variants.

C++ ONNX Runtime (onnxruntime) QuickSRNet Medium super-resolution side-by-side app for MP4 input and fullscreen Wayland display. Decodes the MP4 with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, tees into a passthrough original-video pane and a super-resolution leg running quicksrnetmedium.onnx via qtimlonnx on the CPU execution provider (execution-provider=cpu, optimization-level=disable-all - the portable generation default; this model additionally fails ONNX Runtime session creation with duplicate node names at higher optimization levels, so disable-all is required here), decoded by qtimlpostprocess module=srnet into an RGBA upscaled frame. A qtivcomposer places the original (left pane) beside the super-resolved output (right pane) as two 960x1080 panes and renders fullscreen on waylandsink; composer pad geometry sizes each pane (the render VideoFilter resolution is not pinned). ONNX-CPU C++ sibling of the TFLite super-resolution side-by-side app.

Single-stage image classification C++ app, file-to-file: decodes an MP4 with the Qualcomm hardware decoder (qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec), normalizes to NV12, then tees into a passthrough video leg and a classification leg. The classification leg runs Inception-v3 (inception_v3.onnx) on ONNX Runtime (onnxruntime) via qtimlonnx with the CPU execution provider (execution-provider=cpu, optimization-level=disable-all), decodes the tensor with qtimlpostprocess module=mobilenet, and the top label is merged back via TextFilter + qtimetamux and drawn with qtivoverlay. The annotated stream is hardware-encoded (v4l2h264enc) and written to one output MP4 via h264parse/mp4mux/filesink. The CPU execution provider is built into the ONNX Runtime core and portable, unlike the QNN/HTP provider plugin; optimization-level=disable-all keeps Transpose nodes intact for qtimlonnx layout/caps negotiation; qtimlonnx has no tensors= property so the native ONNX output order must satisfy the module=mobilenet contract. CPU inference runs below realtime, so pipeline.eos(true) and a natural-EOS drain are required for mp4mux to finalize a playable file. ONNX-CPU file-to-file C++ sibling of the TFLite/HTP display classification app.
